subject: Streamlabs Desktop
title: Streamlabs Desktop Alternatives in 2026
description: Nine alternatives to Streamlabs Desktop for gaming streamers: OBS Studio, Meld Studio, Prism, Lightstream, mobile and clip tools, with sourced pricing and limits.
intro: Streamlabs Desktop is the streaming software from Streamlabs, a company that also sells alerts, overlays, tipping and merch for Twitch, YouTube and Facebook. Gaming streamers who leave usually want a lighter or freer encoder, a browser-based setup that spares the gaming PC, or their overlays from a different company. The nine alternatives below cover free desktop software, a cloud studio, mobile and multi-camera apps, and driver tools. We could not read the Streamlabs Desktop product page in full, so we describe it only through the company's main pages.
why_switch: You want a free and open source encoder with no company layer on top, which is what OBS Studio describes itself as.
You would like streaming and multistreaming from one free app, without paying for an add-on tier.
Your gaming PC is busy enough that a browser-based studio that runs in the cloud looks attractive.
You stream from a phone or want multiple cameras, and a desktop-first tool does not fit.
You prefer to keep alerts and overlays with one vendor and the encoder with another.

picks.name: OBS Studio
picks.note: OBS Studio is free and open source software for recording and live streaming on Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13.0 or newer, and Linux. Scenes are built from sources such as window captures, browser windows, webcams and capture cards. Many streamers move here for control and zero cost. You give up the ready-made themes, alerts and tips that Streamlabs bundles, and add those through plugins or other services.

sources.fact: OBS (Open Broadcaster Software) is free and open source software for video recording and live streaming.
The homepage says OBS supports Windows 10 and Windows 11, macOS 13.0 or newer, and Linux.
The homepage describes scenes made of multiple sources including window captures, browser windows, webcams and capture cards.

picks.name: Meld Studio
picks.pricing: Free at $0 a month; Meld Pro $17 a month or $200 billed annually.
picks.note: Meld Studio is free streaming and recording software with multistreaming to every platform at once and 4K recording. Its Meld Spark tool covers interactive overlays and alerts, so the overlay layer is part of the same family. The pricing page lists a free plan and Meld Pro at $17 a month or $200 billed annually. A good fit if you want multistreaming without a paid tier.

sources.fact: Meld Studio is free streaming and recording software with multistreaming to every platform at once and 4K recording.
Meld's pricing page lists a free plan at $0 per month and Meld Pro at $17 per month, or $200 billed annually.
Meld's homepage describes Meld Spark as the tool for interactive overlays and alerts.

picks.name: Prism Live Studio
picks.best_for: Multi-platform streaming plus a mobile app
picks.pricing: Desktop app free; Plus subscription sold in the PRISM mobile app.
picks.note: PRISM Live Studio is free live streaming and recording software with multi-platform streaming and video editing. It runs on Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and on macOS Monterey 12.3 or higher on Apple Silicon. A Plus subscription and Credits are sold in the mobile app. Consider it if you also stream from a phone and want one family of tools across both.

sources.fact: PRISM Live Studio is free live streaming and recording software that provides multi-platform streaming and video editing.
PRISM Live Studio runs on Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and on macOS (Apple Silicon), Monterey 12.3 or higher.
The Plus subscription can be bought through the PRISM mobile app, and Credits are currently available only in the mobile app.

picks.name: Lightstream
picks.pricing: Free tier $0 with logo, 720p, 10 hour limit, 3 scenes; Premium $12 or $9 a month annual.
picks.note: Lightstream is cloud-native streaming software that runs in the browser with no download. The free tier has a Lightstream logo, 720p, a 10 hour limit per stream and up to 3 scenes. Premium is $12, or $9 a month annually, and removes the logo while adding 1080p and 20 scenes. It simulcasts to up to five destinations. The cloud approach spares your PC but caps quality on the free tier.

sources.fact: Lightstream is a cloud-native live streaming software that runs in the browser and needs no downloads.
Lightstream's free tier costs $0 and includes 720p streaming, a 10 hour limit per stream and up to 3 scenes, with a Lightstream logo on all streams.
The Premium plan costs $12, or $9 per month on an annual subscription, and removes the Lightstream logo and adds 1080p and 20 scenes.

picks.name: StreamElements
picks.best_for: Overlays and a bot from a rival suite
picks.pricing: Pricing is not stated on the home page opened.
picks.note: StreamElements is not an encoder in the same sense. It is a cloud platform with overlays, tipping, a chatbot, alerts and merchandise, plus SE.Live, a plugin for OBS Studio. Streamers who leave Streamlabs often pair OBS Studio with StreamElements, which keeps the overlay habit while changing the encoder. Our [StreamElements alternatives page](/alternatives/streamelements) covers that platform in turn.

sources.fact: StreamElements lists overlays, tipping, chatbot, alerts and merchandise among its features for Twitch, YouTube and Facebook Gaming.
SE.Live is a plugin for OBS Studio, and Ground Control is a multistreaming stream management companion app.
The StreamElements home page opened does not show a price.

picks.name: Larix Broadcaster
picks.note: Larix Broadcaster is a free mobile broadcasting app from Softvelum for iOS and Android, aimed at remote contribution streaming. It is not a PC streaming suite and has no overlay layer. It suits a second camera or a field feed rather than a gaming setup. Treat it as an addition to your streaming stack more than a replacement for desktop software.

sources.fact: Larix Broadcaster is free mobile broadcasting software for iOS and Android devices.
The page describes the apps as tools for remote contribution streaming from Android and iOS.
The page links to a documentation reference for the Larix apps.

picks.name: Switcher Studio
picks.pricing: 14-day free trial; plan amounts were not captured.
picks.note: Switcher Studio is multi-camera live streaming software that lets you stream to several platforms. Its homepage and pricing page offer a 14-day free trial. It leans toward camera switching and productions with more than one angle than toward single-screen game capture. Look at it if your streams include a camera crew or IRL segments, and check plan prices on the vendor site.

sources.fact: Switcher Studio is multi-camera live streaming software that lets users stream to several platforms.
The homepage offers a 14-day free trial.
The pricing page is titled Switcher Studio Pricing with a free 14-day trial offer.

picks.name: NVIDIA App
picks.best_for: Capture and broadcast tools for GeForce owners
picks.pricing: No price shown on the download page.
picks.note: The NVIDIA App is the driver companion for PC gamers and creators. NVIDIA lists ShadowPlay and the Broadcast App among its features. It does not replace a full streaming program with scenes and alerts, but for recording gameplay and cleaning up a microphone or camera it covers ground that streamers otherwise add through software. It only applies to NVIDIA graphics cards.

sources.fact: The NVIDIA App is described by NVIDIA as the essential companion for PC gamers and creators, used to keep drivers up to date.
The NVIDIA App download page lists NVIDIA ShadowPlay and the Broadcast App among its features.
NVIDIA's download page for the NVIDIA App is available by region and does not show a price.

picks.name: Medal
picks.pricing: Free to record, edit and share clips on PC, per the homepage.
picks.note: Medal records, edits and shares gaming clips and gameplay videos, and its homepage describes it as free on PC. It does not stream, so it complements Streamlabs Desktop alternatives instead of replacing them. If you are leaving the Streamlabs ecosystem, Medal covers highlights and sharing while a separate encoder handles live output.

sources.fact: Medal is a tool to record, edit and share gaming clips and gameplay videos.
Medal's homepage description says it is free to record, edit and share gaming clips on PC.

how_to_pick: Decide whether you want an encoder, a platform or both. If cost and control matter most, begin with OBS Studio and add services as needed. If multistreaming is the draw, compare Meld Studio and Lightstream, remembering that Lightstream's free tier is capped at 720p. If a second device is in play, look at the phone and multi-camera tools. Our [ranking of streaming software for gamers](/software/best-streaming-software-for-gamers) lays the options side by side.

faqs.a: It is streaming software from Streamlabs, which describes itself as a platform for Twitch, YouTube and Facebook with Streamlabs Desktop, alerts, overlays, tipping and merch. The company's pricing page states it takes zero cut of your donations.

faqs.q: Is there a free alternative with multistreaming?
faqs.a: Meld Studio lists a free plan at $0 a month with multistreaming and 4K recording, and PRISM Live Studio offers multi-platform streaming in a free desktop app. Lightstream also has a free tier, limited to 720p and a 10 hour stream length.

faqs.q: Can I stream without installing software on my gaming PC?
faqs.a: Lightstream runs in the browser and needs no downloads, according to its homepage. The free tier carries its logo and 720p, and Premium removes the logo and adds 1080p.
OBS Studio describes itself as free and open source software for recording and live streaming. Most of the other tools here are closed products with free or paid tiers.

faqs.q: Do I lose my alerts if I switch?
faqs.a: Alerts come from the platform, not the encoder. StreamElements pairs with OBS Studio through its SE.Live plugin, and Meld offers Meld Spark for overlays and alerts, so you can keep an alert layer.
